title: Reasons for Cancellation of “Dialogue and Dissent” Programme at Yale-NUS
what_it_is: Reasons for Cancellation of “Dialogue and Dissent” Programme at Yale-NUS

sections.label: Questions on Yale-NUS programme cancellation
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about reasons for cancelling the Yale-NUS programme and whether it curtails academic freedom and rules on topics.

sentences.text: To ask the Minister for Education (a) what are the reasons and concerns leading to the cancellation of the Yale-NUS programme "Dialogue and Dissent in Singapore"; (b) whether the cancellation of the programme signals a more controlled and rigid education environment in our education institutes; and (c) whether this curtails academic freedom and the critical discourse necessary for academic richness and excellence in our education institutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education whether there are clear rules on what topics and activities are or are not allowed in our autonomous universities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what are the reasons for the cancellation of the "Dialogue and Dissent in Singapore" programme at Yale-NUS College; (b) whether and under what conditions political dissent and activism in the Singapore context is a legitimate topic of academic inquiry in our autonomous universities (AUs); and (c) what can be done to assure AU staff and students that they continue to have the academic freedom to responsibly and critically examine social and political issues in Singapore.

sections.label: Dissent project among 14 projects
sections.summary: The "Dissent and Resistance" project was one of 14 projects in YNC's Week 7 Learning Across Boundaries programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: First, the "Dissent and Resistance" project was one of 14 projects on the slate for YNC’s Week 7 "Learning Across Boundaries", or LAB programme.

sections.label: Activities risked breaking law
sections.summary: A protest placard workshop and a Speakers' Corner visit would have put students at risk of breaking the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Furthermore, specific activities – a workshop to make protest placards and a visit to the Speakers' Corner – would have put students at risk of breaking the law.

sections.label: YNC withdrew project, MOE supported
sections.summary: YNC found insufficient time to revise the project, withdrew it, informed students on 13 September 2019, and MOE fully supported the decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Eventually, YNC concluded that there was insufficient time to revise the project before the start of the Week 7 LAB programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It, therefore, decided to withdraw the project and informed affected students on 13 September 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MOE looked through the itinerary and fully supported YNC's decision.

sections.label: Programme dialogues and personalities
sections.summary: The programme included dialogues with Mr Jolovan Wham and Mr Seelan Palay, and mentions Dr PJ Thum, Ms Kirsten Han and New Naratif.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Besides making protest placards and visiting the Speakers' Corner, the programme included dialogues with personalities, such as Mr Jolovan Wham and Mr Seelan Palay, both of whom have previously been convicted of public order-related offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Dr PJ Thum has publicly suggested that “Singaporeans should celebrate Malaysia’s independence day”, and that Dr Mahathir should “take the lead in lobbying for the promotion of democracy and freedom of expression and inquiry in Southeast Asia”, because Malaysia was “a beacon for many who are struggling for democracy not just in Singapore but in other parts of Southeast Asia.” Both Ms Kirsten Han and Dr PJ Thum have since announced that while the "Dissent and Resistance" project was withdrawn, they will continue their work through New Naratif, an outfit they had set up which receives significant foreign funding.

sections.label: MOE stand on such activities
sections.summary: MOE's stand is that such activities cannot be in schools or IHLs, and political conscientisation is not the taxpayer's idea of education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: He would readily conclude that taking into consideration all the elements and all the personalities involved, this is a programme that was filled with motives and objectives other than learning and education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And MOE's stand is that we cannot have such activities in our schools or IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Political conscientisation is not the taxpayer’s idea of what education means.

sections.label: Educational institutions must obey Singapore laws
sections.summary: All educational institutions must operate within the laws of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: First, all educational institutions must operate within the laws of Singapore.

sections.label: Institutions must not deviate from missions
sections.summary: Educational institutions must not deviate from their missions to advance education and maintain high academic standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Second principle: our educational institutions must not deviate from their missions to advance education and maintain high academic standards.

sections.label: No partisan politics in institutions
sections.summary: Educational institutions should not be misused as a platform for partisan politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Third principle: our educational institutions should not be misused as a platform for partisan politics.

sections.label: Institutions must recognise Singapore's context
sections.summary: Educational institutions must recognise Singapore's cultural and social context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Fourth principle: educational institutions must recognise Singapore's cultural and social context.

sections.label: Limits on academic freedom
sections.summary: Academic freedom is not carte blanche to misuse institutions for political advocacy, which would undermine academic standards and public standing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Academic freedom cannot be carte blanche for anyone to misuse an academic institution for political advocacy, for this would undermine the institution's academic standards and public standing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: At the minimum, they should not undertake activities that expose their students to the risk of breaking the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They should not work with speakers and instructors who have been convicted of public order-related offences, or who are working with political advocacy groups funded by foreigners, or who openly show disloyalty to Singapore.

sections.label: Do not impose or import values
sections.summary: In a globalised world, we must not impose one country's values on others or unthinkingly import values from elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In an increasingly globalised world, we must not try to impose one country’s values and culture on others, or unthinkingly import values and culture from elsewhere into our society.

sections.label: Liberal arts education place
sections.summary: Liberal arts education will continue to have a place in the Singapore education system, as open inquiry and critical thinking are valued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, we value open inquiry and critical thinking amongst our students, and liberal arts education will continue to have a place in the Singapore education system.

sections.label: Project withdrawal and partnership
sections.summary: The withdrawal of this project does not affect the partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The withdrawal of this project does not affect the partnership.

sections.label: Standards and blacklist impractical
sections.summary: The person must meet certain standards beyond course content, and a blacklist is not practical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is not just the course content, but the person has to meet certain standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I do not think it is practical to have a blacklist.

sections.label: Teaching and political activism
sections.summary: Teaching and political activism cannot be conflated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: You cannot conflate your teaching and your political activism.

sections.label: Four principles for institutions
sections.summary: All educational institutions must abide by the four outlined principles rather than their own, while academic freedom is protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The first question on the four principles I outlined are for all educational institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We would not want them to each come up with their own principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But they have to abide by these four which, I think, are eminently reasonable principles while protecting academic freedom.

sections.label: Foreign academic and local academics
sections.summary: A UK academic praised the forum, and steps are being taken to encourage more local academics to join universities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, one foreign academic from the UK who attended it, said that "In the UK, we will never have a forum like this where the university leadership and MOE get together to discuss about the future of universities." On the second question, the Member has raised that several times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are taking various steps and I would be happy to outline maybe on another occasion all the steps we are taking to encourage more local academics to join our universities and make sure we have a strong local core.
